newsitem.title: USA: US stocks may open lower ahead of durable goods.
newsitem.headline: US stocks may open lower ahead of durable goods.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening with a slim loss on Thursday, but the release of August orders for durable goods and weekly jobless claims could boost the market's confidence.

"We're indicated lower but I think it will reverse by the opening if the (data) come in weak, which would support a higher bond market," said Westafalia Investments director of research Peter Cardillo.
Analysts expect a drop of 0.1 percent in August durable goods orders, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
July orders for durable goods rose 1.7 percent.
Weekly jobless claims, expected to edge lower to 328,000 compared with 329,000 last week, will also be scrutinized, according to Bill Meehan, Prudential market analyst.

"Earnings are squarely in front of us though; they are the major focus and if you can't deliver, you will get whacked. We are focusing not so much on specific sectors, but on which companies can deliver strong earnings throughout the sectors," Meehan said.
Meehan said he expected large-cap over-the-counter stocks to continue to lead the market.
Cardillo said he expected strength in bank stocks and possibly in oil stocks after some trace weakness in oil yesterday.
The long bond was off 3/32 to yield 6.94 percent and Standard & Poor's 500 December futures slipped 0.3 to 690.75.
Tokyo stocks moved higher, boosted by strong semiconductors. The key Nikkei-225 closed up 111 to 21,461.
In London, the FTSE-100 lost 9.5 to 3926 in midday trading.
U.S. stocks in London were mixed in quiet trading ahead of the economic data.
The dollar was strong in European trading, but off earlier highs.

Tag Heuer has good timing. The Swiss maker of luxury sports watches known for precision is hitting Wall Street with an initial public offering at a time when shares for other luxury-goods sellers are riding high, according to the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column.
Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc's strong third quarter profits still haven't quashed the rumors that it may be the target of a takeover, according to the New York Times' Marketplace column.
